newsitem.title: FRANCE: French oil industry warns of refinery losses.
newsitem.headline: French oil industry warns of refinery losses.

text.p: The French oil industry association, UFIP, said for the first time on Wednesday that a blockade by striking French truck drivers was starting to have an impact on production at refineries.
"We are starting to see a slight risk of cuts in production at the refineries, especially in the south," an UFIP spokeswoman told Reuters on the 10th day of the strike.
Truckers have singled out the oil industry for the tightest blockades designed to put pressure on the government and persuade haulage bosses to negotiate better pay and conditions.
But refineries have until now been able to maintain their production since only a third of their output usually leaves by road, the rest being transported by pipeline.
The UFIP spokeswoman said all but one of France's 13 refineries were now wholly or partly blocked by protestors' lorries, compared with nine on Monday.

Most fuel depots were also surrounded, bringing the number of petrol stations facing closure or shortages to 1,000 out of a total 18,000 stations in France. Disruption was worst in the south, southwest and northwest, she said.
